homogeneousConstantSectionAndShape.validPart: For one carrier species, I is the cross-section integral of n*q0*v_d. With uniform n, unchanged S and fixed I, the cross-section-averaged directed speed has unchanged magnitude |I|/(|q0|*n*S). For isotropic ordinary ohmic conduction at fixed material state, J = sigma*E and resistivity rho = 1/sigma is fixed.
homogeneousConstantSectionAndShape.missingPremise: Fixed material, temperature and diameter do not by themselves make the vector field or current density uniform within a curved cross-section. The modern text says homogeneous conductor model, but does not identify a one-dimensional thin-wire approximation or distinguish averaged values from local values. Its opening still permits arbitrary bending and states shape independence without that qualification.
homogeneousConstantSectionAndShape.independentCounterexample: Consider an isotropic conductor bent into a toroidal segment with constant circular cross-section radius a, centreline radius R0 > a, angular span Theta, equipotential end faces and insulating side surface. In cylindrical coordinates V = V0 - DeltaV*theta/Theta solves Laplace's equation and has zero normal current through the side. E_theta = DeltaV/(Theta*r), J_theta = sigma*DeltaV/(Theta*r), and the local drift magnitude is J_theta/(n*|q0|). All vary as 1/r across each section, although sigma, n and S are constant and the current is steady. The current is I = sigma*DeltaV/Theta * integral_S(dS/r). Its resistance is rho*Theta/integral_S(dS/r), whereas the straight conductor of the same centreline length L = R0*Theta and section S has resistance rho*R0*Theta/S. For the symmetric finite circular section, the strict convexity of 1/r gives integral_S(dS/r) > S/R0, so these resistances differ. Thus fixed applied voltage need not give exactly unchanged current. This is a reviewer-only analytic counterexample, not an invented lesson exercise.
homogeneousConstantSectionAndShape.oneDimensionalLimit: When a/R0 is small and curvature/contact crowding is neglected, r is approximately R0 throughout each section. Then J is approximately I/S, E is approximately rho*I/S, and R is approximately rho*L/S. In this explicitly stated model, unchanged rho, L, S and applied voltage give unchanged settled I, averaged drift speed and longitudinal field magnitude. Coil inductance affects the switch-on transient, not this settled DC limit.

internalTangentAndExternalObliqueField.derivation: At the insulating side of a stationary ordinary ohmic conductor, J_in dot normal = 0. With isotropic finite conductivity this gives E_in dot normal = 0 just inside the surface. Surface charging removes the internal normal component; it does not remove the external normal component. In the non-inductive stationary regime, a vanishing boundary loop gives continuity of tangential E, while Gauss's law permits a normal displacement-field jump equal to the surface charge density. Hence E_out can have both the same tangential component and a nonzero normal component, and can meet the surface obliquely. In electrostatic equilibrium there is no conduction current, E_in = 0 and the connected conductor is equipotential, so E_out is normal. The modern text correctly separates these cases.
internalTangentAndExternalObliqueField.scope: The lesson's electric-force, isotropic ordinary-conduction model; not a Hall-effect or anisotropic-conductivity claim. Tangency at the side surface does not imply equal field magnitude throughout a finite bend.

surfaceChargesAndPropagation.derivation: A source-terminal charge distribution alone does not in general satisfy the conducting wire's boundary conditions and maintain the required longitudinal field over a long, shaped line. Charges already present along the wire redistribute, and their surface distribution contributes the field required by those boundaries. The source-terminal field is not asserted to vanish at a distance: the modern question correctly asks whether terminal charges alone suffice. The charging disturbance affects successive local regions after finite propagation delay; it does not require the same source electron to reach them. The explicit not-strictly-simultaneous sentence and the following high-speed propagation description preserve this distinction.

It is retained as that source example, not derived as a universal signed-density law for arbitrary branches, polarities, return paths or bends. Actual surface-density profiles depend on the complete circuit geometry and boundary potentials; I and S alone do not determine them.

stationaryFieldAndPotential.derivation: For a fixed macroscopic region, charge continuity gives dQ/dt = I_in - I_out. Equal incoming and outgoing charge over Delta t allows constant surface density while individual carriers keep moving; stationary density is not electrostatic equilibrium. In the chapter's settled DC state with fixed conductor geometry and stationary source/current distributions, B is time independent. Faraday's law then gives curl E = -partial B/partial t = 0, so the electric field in the ordinary circuit region admits E = -grad V. It can be nonzero even though it is a potential field. The source's non-electrical driving forces are not thereby declared conservative.
stationaryFieldAndPotential.assumptionBoundary: This conclusion uses the full stationary, non-inductive circuit state, not constant scalar I alone and not time-independent E alone. It does not apply during switch-on, to externally varying magnetic flux, or to an AC outlet merely because an outlet appeared earlier as an example of charge separation. The modern wording expressly restricts the conclusion to the settled steady state.

findings.title: Homogeneity does not supply the missing thin-wire approximation
findings.statement: The opening permits arbitrary bends and claims shape-independent current under unchanged material, length, section, temperature and supply; the next object then asserts equal field magnitude at all sections and unchanged magnitude after bending. Neither object identifies the required one-dimensional approximation.
findings.whyItFails: Continuity fixes total current and averaged drift speed, not a pointwise uniform field. Even a constant-diameter, constant-resistivity round wire has E and J proportional to 1/r in the finite toroidal bend derived above; its exact resistance is not the straight-wire rho*L/S value. The phrase homogeneous conductor model describes material uniformity and does not remove curvature effects. The literal shape and field claims therefore remain broader than the justified physics.
findings.requiredDisposition: Clarify both linked objects as the settled DC, one-dimensional thin-wire approximation with constant carrier density and resistivity, neglecting appreciable curvature/contact redistribution. Identify the speed and field statements as averaged/longitudinal approximate values within that model, rather than strict local equalities for arbitrary bends. Preserve every source snapshot, original mathematical token, number, reference and zero-task object. This is a modern prose qualification, not permission to edit source formulas or figures.
